Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciated the quick demo and the clarity on routing/quantization options. As discussed, Nimbus is moving forward with a short competitive bake-off to validate latency, cost per 1k tokens, and accuracy on a selection of our production prompts.

I've attached our evaluation template and a redacted MOPA statement (nimbus-mopa-statement.pdf) for your legal/security team. High level asks from our side:

- Success criteria: 95p latency under 120ms for 95% of requests, per-request cost <= $0.003/token-equivalent, and <= 3% model-regression on our quality eval.

Can you confirm next steps, owners, and a proposed timeline? We'd like to start the first round of tests the week of Feb 23 if possible.

Thanks,
Tom
Head of PM
Nimbus Analytics

Subject: Re: Follow-up: competitive bake-off / evaluation criteria

Thanks — looping in details below and attaching a filled execution plan.

Plan (high level):
- Prep (Feb 16-18): infra provision, replay ingestion, create token/embedding buckets, and confirm prompt normalization. Owner: Aditya.
- Canary run (Feb 23-25): 10% of traffic replayed to Redwood + hyperscaler endpoints, collect latency metrics, token counts, and deterministic output diffs on gold prompts. Owner: Aditya + Laura for QA.
- Full run (Mar 1-5): 100% replay across variants (different quantization/mem configs). Owner: Aditya.

Success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: p95 <= 120ms for interactive prompts (seq len ~512); p50/p95 breakdown provided per model.
- Cost: normalized cost per 1k tokens <= $0.003 (we'll normalize across model families).
- Quality: regression <= 3% on our eval set (we'll run pairwise rerank and automated diff).
- Stability: no greater than 0.5% error rate increase (5xx / timeouts) vs baseline.

Technical notes:
- We'll need access to your replay logs in JSONL (one request per line) with input prompt, expected gold answer id, and measured client-side latency. If the logs include API keys masked, provide the mapping table.
- For hyperscalers, we'll use the same request format; please confirm any request/response transformations Redwood will apply (tokenization, prompt truncation, system/msg wrapping).

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-bakeoff-template.xlsx (execution_plan tab filled)

Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
